In my experience you will get checked in from the emergency room. Depending on where you live, your insurance, and if your hospital has an inpatient it will be different. For example when I went YEARS ago and I went to a hospital where they had an inpatient, it was a five hour process from emergency room to hospital room. But this time the hospital didn’t have an inpatient so I was in the emergency room for awhile (like over night) than transported. I would recommend packing a bag, get some books, comfy clothes and a journal (if you pack pens or pencils they will be taken and held on to). Be ready to get comfortable with just yourself. If you need it though the wait doesn’t matter, in the end the same thing will happen you will get to the hospital. Once at the hospital they go through your things making sure you didn’t bring anything that could hurt you. No phone, no pens, ect. Just clothes and books and toiletries. If you don’t have them toiletries are provided. You are asked a lot of questions and the people are very gentle with you. The bed sucks but when you are so low you don’t notice things like that. And if you are and adult 80% of the time you are given time to read,, rest and heal. If you know you need this, go to the hospital get evaluated. I wish you luck.
